floor: WCAG 2.2 Level AA applies to every audience. Internal tools do not get a lighter accessibility pass.
visual: One accent per view. It marks the one thing to look at.
No cards, dashed drop zones, gradient chrome, icon-library status, or filled accent buttons as the default control.
Status is a word, a hairline, or an orb. Gap and warning may use the text markers ⚑︎ and ⚠︎ (U+FE0E). No emoji.
Do not theme the ground brown to feel on brand. Warmth stays in the ink.
operational: Adoption stages do not change event handlers, state, effects, requests, validation, routing, or what a click submits. Behavioral gaps are suggestions.

internal.summary: People inside the organization. Same visual register and the same accessibility floor.
rules: Diagnostics may be visible to an authenticated colleague.
Still do not put internal model names, levels, or scores on a surface a client could read.
Accessibility requirements are identical to external.

external.summary: A surface a client or the public can read.
rules: Hide raw model errors and stack traces.
Do not leak system prompts or internal vocabulary.
The client sees the effect, not the machinery.

hybrid.summary: An external-safe surface, with richer diagnostics only when the person is authenticated.
rules: Default the visible surface to the external rules.
Show diagnostics only after authentication, and only in a region that is not the client view.
Do not let authenticated chrome leak into the external view.
